issue_text: containsBlockerLanguage() is 0% covered and its decision branch in githubReviewBlockers() is never exercised. githubReviewBlockers emits a knowledge candidate when body!="" && (state=="CHANGES_REQUESTED" || containsBlockerLanguage(body)). The only test (TestExtractCandidatesFromGitHubAndSessionCorrectionsWithRedaction) uses state "CHANGES_REQUESTED", so Go's short-circuit means containsBlockerLanguage is NEVER called. A non-CHANGES_REQUESTED review (APPROVED/COMMENTED) whose body contains 'blocker'/'must'/'do not' is supposed to become a knowledge candidate; nothing pins that path.

The title/finding-text fallback in calibrationDisposition() (the switch over strings.Contains(title, "false positive"|"rebutted"|"accepted risk"), lines 211-220) is untested. Every calibration test sets record.Status to a canonical value (false-positive/accepted-risk/rebutted), so the disposition is always resolved by the earlier status/classification loop and the text-fallback switch is dead in tests. This fallback is the only path that turns a finding whose disposition is expressed in prose (not in the Status/Classification fields) into a reviewer-calibration candidate.

alreadyCovered() uses bidirectional substring containment on normalized text: `strings.Contains(haystack, needle) || strings.Contains(needle, haystack)`. The second direction discards a NEW candidate whenever any existing knowledge fact's normalized text is a substring of the candidate's — including short/generic existing facts. A richer, more-detailed new candidate that merely contains an older terse fact is dropped as 'already-covered', losing the added detail; a very short existing fact (e.g. 'run tests') would suppress many unrelated candidates.
